verdicts.why: The `limit: 999` fetch is reduced at :705-714 into the KPI chips (`total: all.length`, draft/sent/accepted/declined counters), so every chip is a count over a capped page rather than the whole set — the exact B12 class.

The 999-row fetch feeds the KPI money memo at :1061-1085 (`outstanding`, `dueThisWeekAmount`, `spend30d` summed and `unpaidCount`/`dueThisWeekCount` counted over `all`), so a tenant past 999 bills shows understated totals.

The tab badge reads `billsData?.meta?.total` (the server's uncapped count) and only falls back to `data.length`, so the displayed number is not derived from the cap — the 999 rows are wasted payload, not wrong arithmetic.

`all` drives both the KPI counters (:559-567) and the money tiles at :571-590 — `openCredit` (a roundMoney reduce over `isOpenCredit` rows) and `issued30Value` — so the credit totals are sums over a 999-row cap.

`dayStart/dayEnd` use host-local `setHours` to bound a `date` column that is written as a UTC calendar stamp, and the window feeds the expense duplicate MATCH at :1182-1192, so a server off UTC silently mis-scopes the dedupe day and re-imports or wrongly skips rows.

`getPriceHistory` maps the 100 rows straight to `{date, unitPrice}` chart points with no total, average or lookup computed over them — a rendering budget (the `asc` order does mean the chart shows the oldest 100, worth a UI note but not arithmetic).

`getCostHistory` likewise returns the 100 movements as plain chart rows (`unitCost`, `avgCostAfter` are per-row columns read from the DB, not re-derived), so nothing is summed or averaged across the capped set.

`getExport` returns the 500 `billingEvent` rows verbatim inside the export payload; no count, sum or match is computed over them here (the truncation is an unlabelled payload budget, not an arithmetic boundary).
Same shape for `rfInvoice`: the 500 rows are passed through into `{ ...invoices }` with no aggregation in this service, so the cap bounds what is rendered/exported rather than any figure.

`diagnoseOrphanedContacts` returns `orphanCount: orphans.length` computed from the `take: 100` read, so the count the caller uses to decide whether to adopt caps at 100 while `adoptOrphanedContacts` then repairs every matching row uncapped.

The 200 candidates are then MATCHED in app code (`candidates.find(c => normalizeNumber(c.invoiceNumber) === target)`, :152-153), so a real duplicate outside the first 200 rows in the date/total window is missed and the invoice is imported twice.

`fuzzyVendorBillCandidates`' 200 rows are consumed by `rows.find(r => r.supplierId === supplierId)` / `totalAgrees` at :329-331 — again a match over a capped candidate set, so a repeat vendor bill can slip past the duplicate guard.
`getJob`'s per-status numbers come from the uncapped `groupBy` at :125-129; the `take: 100` bounds only the `duplicates` array the UI lists, and nothing counts or sums it.
`listJobs` is the "recent migration runs" history list — the 50 rows are returned as-is with no total, count or match derived from them.

`list` applies the `search` filter server-side in the `where` (`rawText: { contains }`) BEFORE the cap, so the cap truncates what is rendered but never breaks the search; no count or sum is taken over the rows.
Per-user `saleDraft` rows for the drafts dock, newest first (the comment says "cap 50 — matches the dock"); no arithmetic, lookup or match is performed over the returned set.

The endpoint returns an honest `meta.total` from a separate `count`, but its consumer `customers/[id]/page.tsx` renders `allOrders.length` (the 50 capped rows) as the "Orders" StatCard value at :2386 and the tab label at :2346, so the customer's order count silently pins at 50 — a count fed by a cap, in two files this PR already touches (reviewer hazard).

`listForTenant` maps the 100 rows into the operator queue rows and returns them; the web page only checks `requests.length === 0` for the empty state and derives no count, total or match from the set.

newHazards.summary: Sweep-confirmed defect INSIDE a touched file, and a direct contradiction of m8's own rule two tabs away: the Profile-tab 'Orders' StatCard renders `allOrders.length` (and the tab label at :2346 renders the same value) from `useCustomerOrders`, which hits GET /customers/:id/orders — customers.service.ts:813-821 reads `take: 50` but returns an honest uncapped `meta.total` right beside it. A customer with more than 50 orders shows 'Orders (50)' forever. m8 ruled 'count chips read meta.total of the filtered query, never the loaded rows' and that fix was applied to Total Invoices at :3570; this sibling count in the same file was left on the capped rows. One-line fix: `ordersResult?.meta?.total ?? allOrders.length` at both sites (the tab label and the StatCard).

Money-discipline miss on the very figures this batch re-based: `outstanding` (:1072, :369), `overdue` (:1077, :374), `advanceBalance` (:1096) and `pendingOrdersAmount` (:1098) are raw float reduces returned unrounded as outstandingAmount/overdueAmount/advanceBalance/pendingOrdersAmount, while `availableCredit` (:1085), `lifetimeInvoiced` and `lifetimeReceived` (:1102-1104) in the same return object all go through roundMoney. The reduces now run over the WHOLE open set instead of a 50/100-row page, so float accumulation is materially more likely (150 rows of 2-dp Decimals can land on 1499.9999999999998). Fix: wrap the four reduces in roundMoney, same as the sibling fields.

The fourth m9 allowlist guard (exportPayments, the CSV twin of listAllPayments) ships with no regression pin — the it.each prototype-key blocks at invoices.service.spec.ts:3482/:3497 cover findAll and listAllPayments only. A future edit can silently revert this site with a green suite. Fix: one more it.each over `service.exportPayments({ sortBy })` asserting the `[{paidAt:'desc'},{id:'desc'}]` fallback.

Orphaned truncation note: `<LedgerTruncationNote truncated={statement?.transactionsTruncated} />` sits under the wallet StatCards, but this page renders no ledger rows at all any more (grep for `transactions` in the file returns only this line and a comment — the `activeCredits` list was replaced by the boolean). The visible list below it is the separately paginated `useBuyerPayments` history, so on a truncated statement the buyer reads 'older entries are not listed in this ledger' next to a list that is in fact complete/paginated. Either drop the note here or move it above an actual ledger.

A second, unlabelled display cap survives M3: `activeCredits` is `.slice(0, 6)` of the ledger's CREDIT_NOTE rows, and the note beneath it (:230) is keyed only to the API's `transactionsTruncated`. A buyer with 9 active credits inside an untruncated ledger sees 6 rows and no label. The count-from-rows defect is genuinely gone (the tile now reads availableCredit), so this is a labelling gap, not a wrong number.

Basis note, not a regression: `lifetimeReceived` is a DIRECT invoicePayment.aggregate, so prisma.service.ts:262-266 injects `tenantId` into its where, while every other payment figure in these methods reads payments through the invoice relation (untenanted) — and InvoicePayment.tenantId is nullable (finance.prisma:319). A legacy NULL-tenant payment row would therefore be missing from lifetimeReceived while still reducing `outstanding`.
